reason: Conflicting polarity: one cited user explicitly rejects Delta, while the proposed policy prefers Delta.
The cited dialogues specify incompatible morning, afternoon, and evening timings; they do not support the proposed concrete default.
The evidence is transaction-local cheapest-option language and does not support the invented 10 percent quality boundary.
Three independent instructions consistently support nonstop by default with at most one stop as fallback; requires final strong-model cross-family review.
Only one citation concerns a window seat; the other two citations concern timing and travel dates.
Only two citations support resort style; a five-star request does not establish resort atmosphere, and the proposed boundary invents an amenity bundle.
The cited minimum thresholds conflict at 3, 4, and 4.5 stars, so they do not support a stable 4.5-star policy.
One citation is about an insulin refrigerator and only two concern balconies; the proposed graph is malformed and unsupported.
